claims.text: What the image looks like Lens-shaped (biconvex) hyperdensity, does NOT cross suture lines; usually temporal → epidural hematoma
claims.quote: Lens-shaped (biconvex) hyperdensity, does NOT cross suture lines; usually temporal Epidural hematoma

claims.text: Example CT: classic lentiform (lens)-shaped hyperdensity that does not extend across suture lines
claims.quote: Classic lentiform (lens)-shaped hyperdensity that does not extend across suture lines.

claims.text: Arterial epidural hematomas classically appear as lenticular-shaped opacities over brain tissue, often in the territory of the middle meningeal artery
claims.quote: Arterial epidural hematomas classically appear as lenticular-shaped opacities over brain tissue, often in the territory of the middle meningeal artery.

claims.text: Buzzword: lens-shaped (biconvex) hyperdensity on head CT → epidural hematoma (does NOT cross sutures)
claims.quote: Lens-shaped (biconvex) hyperdensity Head CT Epidural hematoma (does NOT cross sutures)

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Confirm it is non-contrast (so blood/calcium is not confused with contrast)
claims.quote: Confirm non-contrast (so blood/calcium not confused with contrast).

claims.text: Blood: look for hyperdensity 60-80 HU (epidural / subdural / SAH / IPH / IVH)
claims.quote: Blood - look for hyperdensity 60-80 HU (epidural / subdural / SAH / IPH / IVH).

claims.text: Brain: gray-white preservation; look for sulcal effacement, mass effect, midline shift
claims.quote: Brain - gray-white preservation, sulcal effacement, mass effect, midline shift.

claims.text: Cisterns: basal/suprasellar (5-pointed star); effaced = herniation risk
claims.quote: Cisterns - basal/suprasellar (5-pointed star); effaced = herniation risk.

claims.text: Bone window: skull fracture, sinuses, mastoids
claims.quote: Bone window - skull fracture, sinuses, mastoids.

claims.text: Soft tissue / scalp: hematoma, foreign body
claims.quote: Soft tissue / scalp - hematoma, foreign body.

claims.text: Acute bleeding appears opaque (dense) compared with brain tissue
claims.quote: Contusions and acute bleeding appear opaque (dense) compared with brain tissue.

claims.text: Causes Her chart: middle meningeal artery; lucid interval
claims.quote: Epidural hematoma (middle meningeal artery; lucid interval)

claims.text: Blood between the skull and dura mater (less common than subdural); large or rapidly expanding ones are usually arterial, classically from damage to the middle meningeal artery by a temporal bone fracture
claims.quote: Epidural hematomas are collections of blood between the skull and dura mater and are less common than subdural hematomas. Epidural hematomas that are large or rapidly expanding are usually caused by arterial bleeding, classically due to damage to the middle meningeal artery by a temporal bone fracture.
claims.locator: Pathology of Traumatic Brain Injury, Hematomas

claims.text: Symptoms Symptoms usually develop within minutes to several hours after the injury (the symptom-free period is the so-called lucid interval): increasing headache, decreased level of consciousness, focal neurologic deficits (eg, hemiparesis)
claims.quote: Epidural hematoma symptoms usually develop within minutes to several hours after the injury (the period without symptoms is the so-called lucid interval) and consist of Increasing headache Decreased level of consciousness Focal neurologic deficits (eg, hemiparesis)

claims.text: Pupillary dilation with loss of light reactivity usually indicates herniation; some patients lose consciousness, then have a transient lucid interval, then gradual neurologic deterioration
claims.quote: Pupillary dilation with loss of light reactivity in such patients usually indicates herniation. Some patients who have an epidural hematoma lose consciousness, then have a transient lucid interval, and then gradual neurologic deterioration.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: emergent neurosurgical evacuation
Large or arterial epidural hematomas are treated surgically; small ones thought to be venous in origin can be followed with serial CT
claims.quote: Large or arterial epidural hematomas are treated surgically, but small epidural hematomas that are thought to be venous in origin can be followed with serial CT.

claims.text: Without intervention, patients with arterial epidural hematomas may rapidly deteriorate and die; small, venous ones are rarely lethal
claims.quote: Without intervention, patients with arterial epidural hematomas may rapidly deteriorate and die. Small, venous epidural hematomas are rarely lethal.
